paper.title: Best Arm Identification in Restless Markov Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Best arm identification in restless Markov multi-armed bandits (fixed confidence, known TPMs up to permutation)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Arms are restless ergodic Markov chains (environment = markovian, out of scope from ontology v0.5).
unmapped: each arm is an ergodic finite-state Markov chain evolving whether or not it is selected (restless)
learner knows the set of arm transition probability matrices but not their assignment to arms (permutation unknown)
best arm defined by largest stationary mean of a known function f on the state space
rows of different arms' TPMs are mutually absolutely continuous
learner observes the state of the selected arm
settings.definition_quote: Consider a multi-armed bandit with $K\geq 2$ arms in which each arm is associated with a time-homogeneous and ergodic discrete-time Markov process evolving on a common, finite state space... A decision entity that has knowledge of the set of TPMs of the arms, but does not know the exact mapping of the TPMs to the arms, wishes to find the index of the best arm as quickly as possible, subject to an upper bound on the error probability.

algorithms.name: R-DCR-BAI (R-Delay-Constrained-Restless-BAI, pi*(L, eta, R))
requires_knowledge_of: set of arm TPMs (up to permutation)

symbols.T_star_C: paper's T^*(C): sup over state-action occupancy measures nu on (delays, last observed states, arm) of min over alternatives of sum nu * KL between d-step transition rows (inverse characteristic time)

conditions: rows of TPMs mutually absolutely continuous across arms

source.label: prop:lower_bound
source.quote: Suppose $C\in \mathcal{C}$ is the underlying assignment of the TPMs. Then, \liminf_{\epsilon\downarrow 0}\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\epsilon)}\frac{\mathbb{E}_{C}^\pi[\tau(\pi)]}{\log(1/\epsilon)}\geq \frac{1}{T^{\star}(C)}, where $T^{\star}(C)$ is given by ...

results.notes: Paper's epsilon is the error probability (delta). Holds over all epsilon-correct policies Pi(epsilon). Restated as part of Theorem 4. In the i.i.d.-like case (TPMs with identical rows) it reduces to the Garivier-Kaufmann bound (Lemma 7).

symbols.T_R_unif: T_R^unif(C): min over alternatives of KL drift under the uniform delay-constrained occupancy measure
symbols.T_R_star: T_R^*(C): optimal value of the finite LP with max-delay R constraint
symbols.eta: mixing parameter of the policy in (0,1]
symbols.R: maximum allowed arm delay, integer > K

conditions: rows of TPMs mutually absolutely continuous across arms
initial states drawn from a distribution phi independent of the assignment

source.label: Lemma:almost_sure_upper_bound_for_policy_pi_star
source.quote: Fix $\eta\in (0,1]$, $R\in \mathbb{N}\cap(K, \infty)$, and $C\in \mathcal{C}$. Under the assignment of the TPMs $C$ and under the policy $\pi=\pi^*(L,\eta, R)$, \limsup_{L\to\infty}\, \frac{\tau(\pi)}{\log L} \leq ... \leq \frac{1}{\eta\,T_{R}^{\textsf{unif}}(C) + (1-\eta)\ T_{R}^{\star}(C)} almost surely

results.notes: Almost-sure bound on the stopping time itself; L plays role of 1/delta (Lemma 3: L=1/epsilon gives epsilon-correctness). Compute: the policy solves a finite LP and operates on finite S_R; paper calls it easy to implement, though state space is exponential in K.

source.label: prop:upper_bound
source.quote: Fix $\eta\in (0,1]$, $R\in \mathbb{N}\cap (K, \infty)$, and $C\in \mathcal{C}$. Under the assignment of the TPMs $C$, the policy {\sc $R$-DCR-BAI} satisfies \limsup_{L\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb{E}_{C}^{\pi}[\tau(\pi)]}{\log L}\leq \frac{1}{\eta\,T_{R}^{\textsf{unif}}(C) + (1-\eta)\ T_{R}^{\star}(C)}.

results.notes: Policy is delta-correct with L=1/delta (Lemma 3). Letting eta -> 0 gives 1/T_R^*(C).

bound.regime: L = 1/delta -> infinity, then eta -> 0, then R -> infinity

conditions: rows of TPMs mutually absolutely continuous across arms

source.label: prop:main_result
source.quote: Further, given any $\epsilon>0$, the policy $\pi^{\star}(1/\epsilon, \eta, R) \in \Pi(\epsilon)$ for all $\eta\in (0,1]$ and $R\in \mathbb{N}\cap (K, \infty)$. Additionally, \limsup_{R\to\infty}\ \limsup_{\eta \downarrow 0} \ \limsup_{L\to\infty}\ \frac{\mathbb{E}_{C}^{\pi^\star(L, \eta, R)}[\tau(\pi^\star(L, \eta, R))]}{\log L}\leq \frac{1}{\lim_{R\to\infty}\ T_{R}^{\star}(C)}

results.notes: Theorem 4 also restates the lower bound of Proposition 1 (not duplicated). Matching with the lower bound is shown only when every TPM has identical rows (Lemma 7: T_R^* = T^*), recovering the i.i.d. Garivier-Kaufmann results.
